name: Fat face display
summary: The first type made only for display: a Didone pushed to extreme weight, with stems as thick as half the letter and hairlines kept fine. It shouts from posters and covers, and it fails in text.

philosophy.core_thesis: A letter for a poster is as black as the stem can be while the hairlines keep it readable.
design_principles: Make the stems 0.35–0.5 of the cap height wide and keep the hairlines and serifs fine.
Keep the stroke contrast at 6:1 or more, measured on the o.
Set the stress vertical, as in a Didone, with ball terminals on a, c, f, r and y.
Make the counters small and the round letters wide.
Use it only at 30 pt and more, for a few words.
Set tight: −0.01 to −0.03 em at large sizes, so the black stems form one shape.
anti_patterns: Running text in a fat face
Wide tracking on the lower case
Two fat faces on one page
Light weights from the same family in place of a text face

classification.note: The canon files fat faces with the Didones; this record keeps them apart because their use and setting rules are those of display type.

anatomy.contrast: Extreme: the hairlines are 0.05–0.15 of the stem.
anatomy.serifs: Flat hairline serifs with no bracket or a very small one.
anatomy.terminals: Large ball terminals on a, c, f, g, j, r and y.
anatomy.aperture: Closed: the counters of a, e and s are small slots.
anatomy.key_letters: An a with a large ball and a tiny bowl, a g with a ball ear, and an R with a heavy, straight leg.

metrics.x_height: The x-height is 0.62–0.84 of the cap height; modern display cuts sit high.
metrics.contrast: The side of the o is 6 to 16 times as thick as its top.
metrics.width: Wide: the mean advance of a to z is 0.52–0.66 em.
metrics.figures: Lining figures with large ball terminals.

setting.text_sizes: Do not use it for text; below 24 pt or 32 px the counters fill in.
setting.display_sizes: Set headlines, covers and posters at 36–300 pt.
setting.leading: Set the leading at 0.9–1.05 for headlines.
setting.tracking: Set −0.01 to −0.03 em at large sizes; capitals at 0 to +0.02 em.
setting.case_and_features: Use upper and lower case for warmth or all capitals for a poster; one size and one weight on the page.

pairing.rule: Pair the fat face with a quiet text face of moderate contrast, and give the text much more space than the headline.

pairs.why: It comes from the same vertical-stress family and holds up in small sizes.
The grotesque came from the same posters and keeps the page plain beside the headline.

reference_faces.note: Abril Fatface keeps the classic proportions; Rozha One and Chonburi are fat faces drawn with Devanagari and Thai companions.

evidence.title: Thorowgood fold-out specimen of a fat face, 1825
evidence.credit: Photo by James Puckett (Flickr); Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: Impact with style: the reader stops at a loud headline that still feels classic and editorial.

use_cases: editorial hero titles on the web
avoid_when: The text is longer than a headline.
The page already has a loud display face.

modifiers.how: Bring the weight down to a regular Didone and add white space around the title.
Make the serifs heavy and square, as the Egyptian posters of the same years did.

sources.title: Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (Hartley & Marks, 4th ed. 2012)
